events.title: Covenant w/Israel at Moab
events.notes:
Just before Israel entered Promised Land, Jehovah made a covenant with them to encourage faithfulness to Jehovah and to make adjustments and set forth certain laws necessary for them as they changed from a life of wandering to a settled life.
This covenant ended with the abolition of the Law covenant.

events.notes: 2 Kings 10:30 - Jehovah promised thath 4 generations of Jehus sons would sit on the throne of Israel.

events.title: King - Jeroboam II (Great Grandson of Jehu)
Prophet: Amos
events.notes:
Insight, Volume 1, pages 99-100
"Amos began his career as a prophet two years before the great earthquake that occurred during the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah. At the same time Jeroboam II, son of Joash, was king of Israel. (Am 1:1) Amos prophecy is, therefore, placed sometime within the 26-year period from 829 to about 804 B.C.E., when the reigns of these two kings of Judah and Israel overlapped."

events.title: Prophet: Joel
events.notes:
W07 10/1 p12-15
"In the book bearing his name, Joel says so little about matters other than his message that even the time of his prophecy can only be estimated\uc0\u8203 about 820 B.C.E., nine years after Uzziah became king over Judah. Why is Joel so reticent about himself? The likely reason is that he wants to emphasize the message and not the messenger."

events.title: King Zechariah (Jehus Great-Great-Grandson) (Northern 10-tribe Israel)
events.notes:
Recorded reign of only 6 months.
In 803 BC, Zechariah began to reign in some sense, but evidently the kingship was not fully confirmed as his until c. 792 BC.

events.title: King Shallum (Last of Jehus ruling descendants) (Northern 10-tribe Israel)
Captives taken to Babylon (Ezekiel, Daniel, etc.)
Prophet: ...Daniel
events.notes:
Dont know when he was born, but early in 617 BC Daniel and others were taken into captivity in Babylon, when he was a teenager.

The angels statement to Daniel, As for you yourself, go toward the end; and you will rest, but you will stand up for your lot at the end of the days, seems to imply that his ife was nearing his end (Daniel chapters 10-12; 12:13)

2. The suffering of Jerusalems inhabitants (Ez 4:9-16)
3. The destrcution of Jerusalem and its people (Ez 5:7-12)

Prophecy recorded about 200 years in advance-perhaps 150 years before Cyrus was born:

Is 45:1 - City gates left open
Jer 51:30; Is 13:1, 7 - Babylons military would cease to fight'

events.title: Antiochus desecrates Jerualems temple, Maccabean revolt begins
events.notes:
dp ch 13, para 37
King Antiochus IV sought to show himself mightier than God by eradicating Jehovahs arrangement for worship. Defying Jehovah, he dedicated Jerusalems temple to Zeus, erected a pagan altar there and, 10 days later, a sacrifice to Zeus was offered on the pagan altar. This led to a Jewish uprising under the Maccabees.

events.title: Festival of Dedication instituted (Hanukkah) (John 10:22)
events.notes: In 164 BCE, on the anniversary of Jerusalems desecration three years earlier, Judas Maccabaeus rededicated the temple to Jehovah and the festival of dedication - Hanukkah - was instituted.
